To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new hybrid model and numerical schemes for color image denoosing can remove the mixture impulse and Gaussian noises efficiently.
a new PDE-based image denoising model and the EnoD schemes can remove the impulse and Gaussian noise mixture effectively and efficiently, preserving edges quite well.

we have developed the ENoD difference schemes for the essentially nondissipated MMC and the hybrid MMC-TVM model for image restoration with a minimum introduction of dissipation and that the model and numerical scheme can deal with a mixture of the impulse noise and Gaussian noise efficiently and reliably.
In summary, our research is concerned with
PDES-based image restoration.
the hybridization of the nonconvex TVM with the MMC in order to deal effectively with the mixture of impulse and Gaussian noises.
the hybrid model for image restoration and its numerical implementation for the mixture of the Gaussian and impulse noises.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid model and the new ENoD schemes can be used as a reliable and effective tool for image denoising.
the new hybrid TVM-MMC model is very promising for the PDE-based image denoising.
the new model and schemes are very effective and robust for image denoising and deblurring, and the new model can deal with a wide class of image restoration problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new model can be considered as a new alternative to the TVM model and the new numerical schemes can be considered as new alternatives to the classical schemes.
the hybrid model and ENoD difference schemes are very effective in dealing with the mixture of impulse and Gaussian noise.
the hybrid model is a reliable tool to remove impulse and Gaussian noises simultaneously, and the ENoDs can remove impulse noise efficiently and preserve edges satisfactorily.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybridization of the TVM and MMC models, together with the ENoD scheme, can be a powerful approach to deal with the mixed noise problem in PDE-based image processing.
the hybrid model can remove the Gaussian and impulse noises efficiently and the ENoDs can remove the impulse noise with minimum dissipation.

the ENoD difference schemes for the nonconvex MMC component are capable of removing the impulse noise without introducing dissipation, and thus, they can be combined with the convex TVM component to form an efficient hybrid model for the restoration of images contaminated by the mixture of impulse and Gaussian noises.
